title: supply-chain-lockdown: JWT/SAML/OpenSSL backports and pinning
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Audit and remediate a set of security-sensitive transitive dependencies affecting our auth and SSO surfaces. Scope: (1) backport critical OpenSSL patches into our runtime base images and ensure OpenSSL is at or above our accepted baseline; (2) standardize on maintained JWT and JOSE libraries across services and replace unmaintained forks; (3) swap to a hardened SAML XML parser implementation, pinning versions and adding runtime mitigations; (4) implement CI policies to block high/critical vuln upgrades and publish SBOMs for private deployments. Deliverables: SBOM generation in build, Dependabot configuration + lockfiles, PRs that upgrade/pin libs, runtime compatibility tests, canary rollout, and post-deploy monitoring for auth failures.
comments: 2026-01-21 - Aisha: Kickoff audit completed. Found 7 services using three different JWT libs (jose4j, legacy-internal-jwt, nimbus-jose-jwt). Several SAML integrations still use xml-parser v2.x that lacks recent parsing hardening. OpenSSL on a subset of our dedicated runtime images is at 1.1.1p; need to bring everything to 3.1.x or vendor backports for CVE coverage.

2026-01-28 - Daniel: PoC branch created - github.com/redwood-inference/platform/compare/dep/supply-chain-lockdown (WIP). Replaced legacy-internal-jwt with nimbus-jose-jwt in auth-service and session-gateway. Early unit tests pass; integration tests pending due to SAML XML parser change.

2026-02-02 - Security Eng (Priya Rao): Recommended standardization on nimbus-jose-jwt for Java services (active maintainer + JOSE RFC coverage). For Node services, use jose v4 pinned to 4.15. Added requirement: new libs must support strict signature validation and JWK cache TTL config.

2026-02-10 - Daniel: Raised PRs for OpenSSL base image upgrade. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/images/pull/412 - includes rebuild of runtime containers and smoke tests. Noted increased image size by ~12MB. Performance regression tests scheduled.

2026-02-18 - QA (Marta): Integration tests against SAML IdP failing with parser change; found edge case: undocumented NameID format used by partner 'AcmeRetail'. Created reproducer and confirmed fixable by allowing permissive NameID fallback with logging. Added acceptance test case.

2026-02-22 - Daniel: Implemented permissive NameID fallback gated by feature flag 'saml.nameid_fallback' (default false for canary). Added structured telemetry for SAML parsing errors to trace SSO failures by partner.

2026-02-26 - Security: Enabled Dependabot alerts + auto PR generation for direct deps. Added manual approval required for any auto-generated PR that touches oauth/jose/saml libs. Config in .github/dependabot.yml (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3456).

2026-03-01 - Ops (Lin): Canary rollout started for auth-service, 5% traffic to upgraded runtime with OpenSSL 3.1.x and pinned JWT libs. No regressions observed in 48h for latency P50/P95; slight increase in CPU (~4%). Keeping canary for full 72h.

2026-03-04 - Daniel: Security review board completed. Action items: (a) add SBOM output to nightly builds (CycloneDX), (b) include artifact signatures for private deployments, (c) update onboarding docs for SSO partners about NameID fallback behavior. Security review required: true.

2026-03-05 - Aisha: Next steps - address ACME partner opt-in for permissive fallback, finish rolling out container rebuilds to Dedicated clusters, and schedule a mid-March postmortem with partner SREs if outages occur. Marking ticket for release 'platform-2026.03-security'.
